record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Domain-dependent upper bounds for classical smoothness classes
record.original_question: Let k be a fixed positive integer and let F_d^k(D_d) be the class of functions f:D_d -> R on a domain D_d subset R^d of volume 1 such that every mixed partial derivative D^alpha f of order |alpha| <= k satisfies ||D^alpha f||_infty <= 1. For which domains D_d does the worst-case integration error admit an upper bound of the form e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) <= c_k d n^(-k/d), and how can one explicitly construct algorithms that achieve this rate on those domains?

evidence.quote: Open Problem: For which Dd do we have upper bounds of the form e(n,Fkd (Dd)) <= ckdn-k/d ? Construct algorithms that achieve this bound for such domains.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $k$. For each dimension $d \geq 1$, let $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a (measurable) domain of Lebesgue volume $1$, and let
$$F_d^k(D_d) := \{\, f : D_d \to \mathbb{R} : \|D^\alpha f\|_\infty \le 1 \text{ for every multi-index } \alpha \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^d \text{ with } |\alpha| \le k\,\}.$$
For an algorithm $A_n$ that approximates $\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx$ using at most $n$ function evaluations of $f$, define the worst-case error
$$e(A_n, F_d^k(D_d)) := \sup_{f \in F_d^k(D_d)} \Bigl| \int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx - A_n(f) \Bigr|,$$
and let $e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) := \inf_{A_n} e(A_n, F_d^k(D_d))$ be the optimal (deterministic) $n$-th minimal worst-case error over all such algorithms.

Problem. Characterize the family of domains $D_d$ (as $d$ varies) for which there exists a constant $c_k > 0$, depending only on $k$, such that
$$e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) \le c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d} \qquad \text{for all } n, d \ge 1,$$
and for each such admissible family $\{D_d\}$ construct an explicit sequence of algorithms attaining this rate.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on optimal numerical integration algorithms. While the bound is known for the unit cube via classical quasi-Monte Carlo/composite rules, a general characterization of domains $D_d$ of volume 1 admitting the $c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d}$ rate, together with explicit constructive algorithms, does not appear to have been resolved in subsequent literature.
